notes.text: This checkout has a real durable order engine, but no real-money payment path. Debug always pairs simulated payment with simulated hardware; mixed real/simulated boundaries are rejected.
Orders freeze device-minted cup IDs, recipes, choices and integer-halalah prices. Payment operations have stable IDs, exact amounts, parent relationships and provider references.
Persist-before-effects is the money-safety boundary. Provider adapters own protocol/session handling, correlation, deduplication, currency scaling and reconciliation—not a second financial ledger.
Pending refunds need not stop remaining prepaid cups if fresh machine readiness permits. A refused refund remains due and needs review.
A cup observed at pickup is already made: per-cup completion starts then, without waiting for customer collection. Later faults cannot erase that evidence.
Unknown physical outcome leaves that cup unresolved, marks remaining queued cups NotStarted, and requests exact-price refunds for those prepaid unstarted cups. Unknown funding is not a decline.
Restart converts outstanding commands and unused approvals to uncertainty without replay. Payment reconciliation is read-only; physical reconciliation and human resolution remain future work.

The existing TCN VendStateMachine/MachineSession path remains separate from the debug order adapter. A future production OrderMachine must use the single machine-session owner; TCN command acknowledgment is not proof of a drink.
The per-cup policy accommodates approval/result-style providers but is not an MDB implementation or proof a reader supports the required behavior. Real adapters need hardware/provider qualification.
Backend upload is unfinished and is not in the vend path. Leaving the customer screen does not discard unresolved financial ownership.

assumptions: “Now” means the current local checkout, not archived Jetinno designs or a future production deployment.
The payment-policy branches describe the implemented core behavior; their calls still pass through the coordinator and durable ledger shown above.
